subject: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap and MAP items (FintechCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>
Cc: Chris O'Neil <chris@fintechco.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap and MAP items (FintechCo)

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciate you and Chris taking the time. I wanted to follow up with a short recap of the performance/SLO items we discussed and propose a mutual action plan (MAP) to get you the data you need for decisioning.

SLO checklist (from our conversation):
- Target latency: P95 end-to-end request (server-side) <= 300ms for non-streaming generation.
- Streaming: support token-level streaming with first-byte latency <= 150ms and steady-state chunk intervals <= 80ms.
- Throughput: sustain 800 concurrent requests (peak) with average request size ~400 tokens.
- Concurrency: guarantee 150 concurrent active model streams without degradation.
- Error budget/availability: 99.9% uptime SLA and token-level error rate < 0.1% monthly.

Proposed next steps (MAP):
1) SE-led perf plan: Rafael to run a short spike (2–3 days) to reproduce representative workloads and collect P50/P95/P99 latencies.
2) Streaming test: we'll share a streaming-test-plan.xlsx; FintechCo to provide 3 representative prompts and expected output length distribution.
3) SLA/contract decision criteria: you confirm whether P95 <= 300ms + streaming thresholds above are gating for Proof-of-Value.
4) Follow-up QBR: schedule a 30-min check-in next week to review results and tradeoffs (quantization, batching, cost).

I've attached a concise post-demo SLO checklist and the streaming test plan. Rafael — can you confirm ETA for the perf spike and any infra requirements?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: post-demo-slo-checklist.pdf
Attachment: streaming-test-plan.xlsx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap and MAP items (FintechCo)

Thanks Marissa — happy to lead the spike. Quick technical notes and ask so we scope tests correctly:

Scope & approach:
- We'll run two spikes: (A) non-streaming generation (batched) to measure end-to-end P50/P95/P99 and throughput; (B) streaming spike to measure first-byte latency and steady-state chunk timing.
- Test infra: prefer to run on a dedicated Redwood Dedicated instance matching our production configuration (A100-ish profile). If FintechCo wants to run on their Dedicated or Private environment, let us know (we can provide a config).

Inputs needed from FintechCo:
- 3 representative prompts (simple, medium, complex) and expected token length distribution (or sample outputs).
- Expected concurrency pattern (e.g., steady 150 concurrent streams, or spiky bursts to 800 QPS).

Success criteria we'll report back:
- P95 non-streaming latency <= 300ms (pass/fail) and cost estimate per 1M tokens at observed batch sizes.
- Streaming: first-byte <= 150ms and chunk interval <= 80ms for 95% of streaming tokens.
- Resource utilization and recommended config (batching, kv cache, quant profiles).

ETA & duration: I can start the spike on Mon 9 Mar and have initial results within 48 hours.

I'll stand up the test harness and share a Drive link with raw results and graphs.

-Rafael
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

From: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris O'Neil <chris@fintechco.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap and MAP items (FintechCo)

Thanks Marissa and Rafael — this aligns well with our procurement checklist. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Decision gating: our internal committee will require P95 <= 300ms for non-streaming and first-byte <= 200ms for streaming (we may be able to accept up to 200ms first-byte if everything else looks solid).
2) Concurrency pattern: realistic load is spiky — baseline 150 concurrent active users, with bursts up to 800 concurrent requests for 30–60s during batch runs. We can provide a 24-hr playback trace from production next week.
3) Data locality: tests should be run in us-west-2 to reflect prod traffic.

Attached is a short internal SLO doc that maps our expectations to the items you listed. We'll also provide 3 prompt templates and the playback trace by Tue 10 Mar.

Questions for Rafael: do you need model variants (.e.g, quantized vs fp16) to run both, or will you run on the same checkpoint and then simulate quantized behavior? Also any specific headers we need to include for streaming hooks?

Best,
Alice
VP Product | FintechCo
alice@fintechco.com
Attachment: fintechco-internal-slo.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Chris O'Neil <chris@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance / SLO recap and MAP items (FintechCo)

Perfect — thanks Alice. Quick confirmation and next steps from Redwood: 

- Rafael will start the perf spike on Tue 10 Mar (US-WEST-2) and produce a results deck within 48 hours.
- FintechCo to share: 3 prompt templates + 24-hr playback trace by Tue 10 Mar EOD. Please upload to the Drive folder (I shared the link above) or reply with attachments.
- Decision criteria noted: P95 <= 300ms, streaming first-byte target <= 200ms (we'll aim for 150ms and call out tradeoffs).
- I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Thu 12 Mar to review initial results and next MAP items (contractual SLA language and sizing).

If that looks good, I'll send a calendar invite for Thu and Rafael will attach the test harness and config before starting.

Thanks — looking forward to the spike and getting you a concrete performance/cost tradeoff.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
